activity.message:
Merge pull request #2 from kosuke-satake/feat/firmware-control-core

Add hardware-independent firmware control logic

Merge pull request #1 from kosuke-satake/feat/initial-structure

Set up initial repository structure and design docs

Document PlatformIO and the firmware test command

Record the choice of PlatformIO, the rule that hardware-independent
logic stays in firmware/lib with host tests, and mark Stage 1 as in
progress in both READMEs.

Run firmware host tests in CI

The tests use PlatformIO's native environment, so they can run on every
pull request without an ESP32 attached.

Add command timeout detection

The body must stop the motors when velocity commands stop arriving. The
timeout starts expired, so the motors stay stopped until the first
command, and latches once expired so a long silence cannot look short
after millis() wraps around.

Add a PID controller for wheel speed

Includes feedforward, derivative on measurement to avoid kicks when the
target speed jumps, and anti-windup so a stalled wheel does not leave a
large integral behind.

Add differential-drive kinematics with host tests

The body receives only linear and angular velocity, so it needs its own
conversion to left and right wheel speeds. When a wheel would exceed its
limit, both wheels are scaled together to keep the turning radius.

The PlatformIO project starts with a native environment only, so the
logic can be tested without hardware; the ESP32 environment follows
once the board is chosen.

Note the use of AI assistants in the README

Commits no longer carry AI co-author trailers, so state the use of AI
tools once in the README instead of hiding it.

Require agents to ask before important decisions

Agents should check with the maintainer instead of pressing on, and
must stop and ask when unsure whether something is a secret rather
than commit it and report afterwards.

Keep motor driver inputs stopped during ESP32 reset

The hardware watchdog only makes the robot safe if a reset actually
stops the motors. While the ESP32 resets or boots its pins float and
some may toggle, so the driver inputs need to default to stopped in
hardware.
